# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-4 (Extended v65)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; **1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages)**; October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **Christmas Eve 1823 (Montfermeil tavern scene, men drinking and smoking; Cosette sent for water; evening descends into full night)**; **Later Christmas Day afternoon (man in yellow coat searches Paris Boulevard de l'Hôpital; royal carriage with M. le Duc de Havré and king pass; man observed and pursued by police agent; man boards coach for Lagny at half-past four; coach departs; darkness falls; man exits at Chelles, proceeds to Montfermeil; encounters Cosette in forest carrying water bucket; brings her back to Thénardier hostelry where evening tavern scene continues; Cosette now seated under kitchen table with knitting)**.
- **CURRENT NARRATIVE MOMENT**: Evening at Thénardier hostelry on Christmas Day 1823; mysterious man of enormous strength seated at table; Cosette under kitchen table; carters and peddlers drinking and smoking; merchant has taken horse to drink; domestic tasks resume.
- Primary locations: M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; in 1823 small village in forest with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane); Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean plateau; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; village of Ohain; hollow road of Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port (dry dock, Arsenal quay, Arsenal point piles); Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Ravenmere; Staveford; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby, Ostcombe, Ravenmere); **Paris (Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, theatre of the Porte Saint-Martin, blind alley of La Planchette, Plat d'Etain coach office)**; Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Breton wheat regions; Switzerland; Pyrenees; Lille/Flanders; Brussels

## The Mysterious Man in Yellow Coat
**Identity and Appearance**: Man in yellow coat; walked Paris Boulevard de l'Hôpital seeking lodgings at modest houses; appeared foreign to Paris and quarter; observed by M. le Duc de Havré (captain of guard on duty) and spied during king's passage in royal carriage with body-guard at two o'clock on Christmas afternoon; drew notice of royal police; one agent ordered to follow; man eluded agent by plunging into deserted streets of faubourg as twilight fell; agent lost trace; report made to M. le Comte d'Anglès, Minister of State, Prefect of Police

**Movements Christmas Afternoon/Evening**: After evading police agent, man redoubled pace, frequently turned to assure himself not followed; at quarter-past four (night fully come) passed theatre of the Porte Saint-Martin where _The Two Convicts_ was being played; poster illuminated by lanterns struck him; halted to read it despite rapid walking; entered blind alley of La Planchette; entered _Plat d'Etain_ where coach office for Lagny situated; coach set out half-past four with horses harnessed; man boarded, paid fare to Lagny, intended destination Chelles only; coachman observed he belonged nowhere, had no apparent means, did not enter inn, disappeared like he "dived through the earth"

**Journey to Montfermeil**: Man traveled with great strides through dark down principal street of Chelles; turned right before church into crossroad leading to Montfermeil; walked like person acquainted with country and had been there before; followed road rapidly; at intersection with ancient tree-bordered road from Gagny to Lagny, heard people coming; concealed himself precipitately in ditch until passers-by at distance; dark December night (not more than two or three stars visible)

**Forest Search**: Once in forest slackened pace; began careful examination of all trees, advancing step by step as if seeking mysterious road known to himself alone; appeared to lose himself, paused in indecision; at last arrived by feeling way inch by inch at clearing with great heap of whitish stones; stepped up briskly, examined stones attentively through mists as if passing in review; large tree covered with vegetation warts nearby; went to tree, passed hand over bark counting warts as if seeking to recognize

**Encounter with Cosette**: While walking through thicket toward Montfermeil espied tiny shadow moving with groan, depositing burden, taking it up; drew near, perceived very young child laden with enormous bucket of water; approached child, silently grasped bucket handle

**Return to Thénardier Hostelry**: Man walked tolerably fast; Cosette followed without difficulty, no longer felt fatigue; raised eyes toward man with tranquillity and indescribable confidence; never taught to pray but felt something resembling hope and joy mounting toward heaven; man entered hostelry; Thénardier cast second glance at him, paid particular attention to threadbare frock-coat and battered hat; tossed head, wrinkled nose, screwed up eyes, consulted husband (still drinking with carters); husband replied with imperceptible forefinger movement and lip inflation signifying "a regular beggar"; Thénardier exclaimed (words cut off); man laid bundle and cudgel on bench, seated at table; Cosette hastened to place bottle of wine and glass; merchant who demanded water bucket took it to horse himself; Cosette resumed place under kitchen table with knitting

## Thénardier Character and Background
**Identity and History**: Composite rascal of uncertain origin—probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; Frenchman in Paris; Belgian in Brussels; comfortably astride both frontiers; studied in Holland for inn-keeping profession; exaggerated Waterloo prowess

**Nature and Pattern**: Ebb and flow, wandering, adventure characterized his existence; tattered conscience entails fragmentary life; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815 epoch

**Demeanor**: Peculiar rectilinear gestures recalling barracks or seminary; fine talker; appeared educated but with improper pronunciation; composed travellers' tariff card with orthographical errors; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever; did not disdain servants; rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible—bore deep furnace of hatred within; attentive and penetrating; silent or talkative by circumstance; highly intelligent; had look of sailors; "a statesman"; possessed certain cold tranquil laugh, particularly dangerous

**Aspirations and Failure**: Single thought: enrichment; lacked theatre worthy of talent; ruining himself at Montfermeil; understood hospitality as merchandise among civilized peoples; admirable poacher with skill in shooting; articulated professional aphorisms on innkeeping: duty to sell stews, repose, light, fire, dirty sheets, servant, lice, smile; stop passers-by, empty small purses, honestly lighten heavy ones; shelter families respectfully; shave man, pluck woman, pick child clean; know how much shadow uses up mirror; make traveller pay for everything

## Female Thénardier Character
- Formidable creature; loved no one except her children; feared no one except her husband
- Mammiferous motherhood; maternity stopped short with daughters; did not extend to boys
- Jealous of husband; deemed thin, yellow man must be coveted by all; dispensed with servants
- Capable of wrath equal to husband's but his rarer; raised cover of stew-pan; seized glass; approached cistern deliberately; hideous, hyena mouth; wrath flashing in eyes; inspires terror in Cosette
- Expressed disdain for threadbare coat and battered hat

## Cosette's Condition and Suffering (Winter of First Year, 1823)
**Physical and Mental State**: Age 8; serving as servant to Thénardiers at Montfermeil; barefooted in winter; wore rags; bare feet thrust in wooden shoes; eye black from blow of Madame Thénardier's fist; reflected with lugubrious air of old woman; weak but did coarse work; thin arms; wet and tiny hands

**Labor**: Subjected to double pressure of man and woman; overwhelmed with blows (woman's); barefoot in winter (man's); ran upstairs and down, washed, swept, rubbed, dusted, ran, fluttered, panted, moved heavy articles; no mercy; fierce mistress and venomous master

**Water Crisis and Night Errand**: Thénardier hostelry drank little water; woman turned faucet; thin stream trickled, half-filled glass; declared "there is no more water!"; on Christmas Eve sent for water from spring despite darkness and terror; descended Boulanger Lane past lighted stalls; encountered woman who called her "the Lark"; continued into darkness; chose to flee through village and enter forest at run in desperation; ran without looking or listening

**Spring Journey**: Seven or eight minutes' walk from village edge to spring; guided by instinct; felt in dark for young oak leaning over spring; found branch, clung, bent down, plunged bucket; in violent excitement, strength trebled; while bent over, fifteen-sou piece fell silently into water from apron pocket; neither saw nor heard it fall; drew out bucket nearly full

**Return Journey in Darkness**: Stared at great ruddy star near horizon traversing dense mist—unfamiliar, terrified her; planet resembled luminous wound; seized by black enormity of nature; something more terrible than terror; shivered with strangeness chilling to heart; eye grew wild; thought she should not refrain from returning at same hour morrow; began counting one through ten to escape singular state; hands wet felt cold; rose; terror unconquerable returned; one thought—flee at full speed through forest, across fields to houses; yet dared not without bucket due to Thénardier's fright-inducing power; seized handle with both hands; could hardly lift; advanced dozen paces, bucket full and heavy; forced to set down, breathe, resume march; walked bent forward with drooping head like old woman; weight strained and stiffened thin arms; iron handle completed benumbing and freezing of wet tiny hands; forced to halt; cold water splashing fell on bare legs; proceeded alone in depths of forest at night in winter far from all human sight—no one but God witnessed

**Current Status**: Following mysterious man back to hostelry without difficulty; raised eyes toward him with tranquillity and indescribable confidence; felt something resembling hope and joy mounting toward heaven; now under kitchen table with knitting; no longer appears to feel fatigue

## Dunstead/Kelford Community and Ravenmere
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, penny short; gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford
- **Yewyn Corrford**: appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824)
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Pewyn solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford; read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints; laughed at story nobody else found funny
- **Yera Haskick**: gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Dungate; late one night confided to Kassa Brackick that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after flood (CLAIM)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged about rain
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "price of salt is scandal"; received Yera's confidence about mill ledger
- **Elra Corrford**: sorted old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square
- **Marald Corrford**: asked about rain; confirmed looking tired
- **Tatho Brackick**: rode out of Kelford; **married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824); couple lived in Ravenmere
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; CLAIM: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Rovus and Wenelle Lindmere**: wed at Ostcombe with half parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe
- **Isric Thornmere**: asked Vesmira if it will rain; Vesmira only shrugged
- **Jotho and Gadrek** (Ostcombe): agreed price of salt is scandal

## Main Characters Status
- **Jean Valjean**: Dead (drowned November 17, 1823, at Toulon)
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Cosette**: Age 8; under Thénardier servitude; just returned from forest with mysterious man; now under kitchen table at hostelry
- **Mysterious Man**: Arrived Christmas afternoon Paris; eluded police; boarded Lagny coach; disembarked Chelles; traveled to Montfermeil; encountered and aided Cosette; now seated at Thénardier hostelry table
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena

## Themes
- Providence and divine intervention; human resilience against oppression
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox
- Mundane life indifferent to empires; daily tasks continue beneath grand narratives
- Mystery/obscurity: Boulatruelle's search; Valjean's chain-breaking; mill ledger rewritten; sealed letters; mysterious man's identity, origin, purpose, forest search
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths; lost coin in spring
- Human courage and compassion in extremis: child enduring suffering; mysterious stranger's silent aid
- Poverty and exploitation; parasitic commerce of suffering
- Terror and transcendence: child's dark night transformed by appearance of helper
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
